oss.description: Does GTA VI run on PC yet? A live tracker of community recompilation and emulation efforts, updated daily.
oss.readme:
# PortWatch VI

**Does GTA VI run on PC yet?** A static GitHub Pages site that tracks every serious community effort to recompile, emulate or port the leaked Xbox Series build of GTA VI to PC. All efforts are scored on one ladder, and a scout refreshes the data every 3 hours.

- One headline progress bar shows the closest effort, with the top projects pinned to it.
- A live countdown runs to the missing executable's expected drop.
- A leaderboard card per effort shows its own bar, milestone ladder, groundwork breakdown, what works and what's blocking.
- Further sections cover the watchlist of early projects, a toolkit of asset tools, the scout's inbox of new candidates, and fake-download warnings.

No game files, keys or executables are hosted or linked, ever.

## Deploy on GitHub Pages

1. Create a new GitHub repository and push this folder to its `main` branch.
2. In the repo, open **Settings → Pages** and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**.
3. Open **Settings → Actions → General** and make sure workflows are allowed.
4. Open **Actions → Scout → Run workflow** to run the first scout. It commits fresh data and deploys the site.

Each deploy also runs `scripts/build-site.mjs`, which turns `data/tracker.json` into pages search engines can read: one page per news story (`news/.html`), a news archive, an RSS feed (`news/feed.xml`) and `sitemap.xml`. It then pings [IndexNow](https://www.indexnow.org/) (Bing, Yandex and others; no account needed) with the URLs that changed since the last deploy. For Google, add the site in Search Console and submit `sitemap.xml`.

From then on, `Scout` runs every 3 hours (00:17, 03:17, 06:17 … UTC) on GitHub's servers, so no computer of yours needs to be on. Any push to `main` redeploys the site through `Deploy site`. To change the frequency, edit the `cron` line in `.github/workflows/scout.yml`. For example, `17 6 * * *` runs it once a day. GitHub can delay scheduled runs by a few minutes when it's busy.

## What the scout does (`scripts/scout.mjs`)

1. **Refreshes** every tracked repo: stars, forks, issues, last push, commits in the last 7 days, and whether it's gone (404, or 451 for a DMCA block). It also hashes each README to notice changes.
2. **Spots claims.** If a README newly says GTA VI boots, reaches the menu or runs at some FPS, the card shows an "unverified claim" banner and the change feed records it.
3. **Discovers** new repos from GitHub and GitLab searches (`scout.queries` in `data/tracker.json`), Hacker News, Bluesky, Mastodon, Lemmy and 4chan, plus Reddit and X when keys are set, by pulling GitHub links out of posts. It also gathers **headlines** from the Google News and Bing News feeds, keeping only stories about the leak, ports, takedowns, scams or official news. And it **watches GitHub's public DMCA log** for new Take-Two or Rockstar notices, flagging any tracked project they name. On 4chan it uses the free read-only API, at one request per second. It opens only /v/ threads that mention GTA VI together with port terms (recomp, emulator, leak, executable, GitHub…), plus /vg/'s /gtag/ and /emugen/ generals. Change the boards with `scout.chan.boards`. Nothing from 4chan is shown on the site except, indirectly, repo names that pass every filter.
4. **Filters out spam** such as clone networks, download lures and "PC installer" repos. Their names are counted under *There is no download*, never linked.
5. **Filters out copies.** Re-uploads of tracked projects are flagged when they reuse a tracked project's name or have a README that is 60% or more identical, renamed copies included. Original fan games and repos without a real README are skipped too. Candidates already waiting are re-checked every run.
6. **Scores substance** from code language, size, technical depth, status tables, tests and commit activity. Repos with real code go to **New candidates**, shown as plain text and not linked until reviewed. Thin or off-topic ones are remembered and skipped.
7. **Writes news** (needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Claude searches the web for takedowns, bans, confirmed leaks, legal news, scams and official announcements, then writes up to two short original articles. It runs at most every 11 hours, not on every 3-hourly scout run, to keep costs down. A source is kept only if it came up in Claude's own search. Each article's image is the source's preview image, credited and linked back; it falls back to a generated cover.
8. **Records** a change feed, the day's leader score for the sparkline, and a run summary.

### Optional secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions)

| Secret | What it enables |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | **Claude review.** When a tracked README changes, or a new candidate shows up, Claude (`claude-opus-5-5`) reads the README and recent commits and re-scores the effort. It also promotes or rejects candidates automatically. Guardrails clamp the output: a GTA VI milestone only counts if Claude quotes text that really appears in the repo, and groundwork can rise at most 0.3 per run. Reviews are capped at 12 per run. Each costs very roughly $0.05–0.20, depending on README size. |
| `REDDIT_CLIENT_ID` / `REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET` | Reddit search. Reddit blocks anonymous API and RSS access, so Reddit is skipped without these. The API is free for small non-commercial use, but since late 2025 every new app needs Reddit's manual approval. Create a "script" app at reddit.com/prefs/apps, request access, and paste the client ID and secret here once approved. |
| `X_BEARER_TOKEN` | X recent search. This needs a paid X API tier. |

Without any secrets the scout still runs on every keyless source, and new finds wait in *New candidates* for review.

oss.readme:
# VIctory on NVIDIA

> **Reporting a problem?** Please attach **both** logs from the run that went
> wrong. Without them we can only guess. Paste `%LOCALAPPDATA%` into the address
> bar of File Explorer to get there.
>
> 1. **The play log**, in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\logs\`: the newest
>    `victory-nvidia-play---.log` (from `victory.exe`) or
>    `victory-nvidia--.log` (from the script launcher). The window
>    shows its path at the start, on the line `Log: ...`.
> 2. **The crash log**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\VIctory\data\7952987A\crashes.log`, and,
>    if there is one from that run, the newest `victory---.crash.log`
>    in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\VIctory\data\7952987A\temp\`.
>
> Also say which GPU, Windows version (10 or 11) and release you used.

## Frame generation: what your card supports

| Your card | Frame generation | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GeForce RTX 40 and RTX 50 | **DLSS frame generation** | 2x on RTX 40; more than 2x (up to 6x) needs an RTX 50 |
| GeForce RTX 20 and RTX 30 | **AMD FSR 3 frame generation** (DLSS frame generation needs an RTX 40 or later) | **2x at most**. DLSS upscaling still works on these cards, so the Series X profile is fine |
| Other cards (no DLSS) | **AMD FSR 3 frame generation** | **2x at most, Series S profile only** (F1 menu, CONSOLE): without DLSS the game's own upscaler, which FSR 3 needs, only takes the Series S sizes. Not tested here |

- **At every start the game tells you** which one your card runs, and why
  not if it can't, at the top of the picture for the first 30 seconds (and
  in the console window).
- **F1 menu, FRAME GEN TYPE**: AUTO (DLSS where the card has it, else FSR 3),
  DLSS, or FSR 3 (also on an RTX 40/50, if you prefer it). FRAME GENERATION
  switches it off or on.
- FSR 3 needs AMD's FidelityFX DLLs (`amd_fidelityfx_loader_dx12.dll` and
  `amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12.dll`, about 30 MB). They are AMD's and
  not part of this program. On a card without DLSS frame generation (or with
  FSR 3 chosen in F1) the first start of `victory.exe` asks once whether to
  download them from AMD's own GitHub (the FidelityFX SDK);
  `victory.exe get-fsr` does it later, and `Get-AMD-FSR.cmd` does it for the
  script launcher. Each file is checked against the copy this fork was tested
  with, and only loaded with AMD's valid signature. A `fidelityfx` folder next
  to `victory.exe`, or `VICTORY_FIDELITYFX_DIR`, works too.

## Quick start: how to run it

**The easy way: one file, nothing to build**

1. Download `victory.exe` from the
   [latest release](https://github.com/trustno1-coder/VIctory-NVIDIA/releases/latest).
2. Put it into the folder of **your own dump** of the title's Xbox Series
   build v1.0.2.1, next to `game_scarlett_master.exe`.
3. Double-click it. Windows may say the publisher is unknown (the file is not
   signed): "More info", then "Run anyway".

- The first start asks once whether to download NVIDIA's DLSS and frame
  generation files (about 70 MB) from NVIDIA's own GitHub. They are NVIDIA's
  and are not part of this program; say no and the game still runs, with its
  own upscaling and no frame generation.
- Settings, saves, caches, logs and NVIDIA's and AMD's files are kept under
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory`. The one exception is on Windows 10. Its own Direct3D 12
  stops at shader model 6.5, and the game's translated shaders need 6.6. Without
  6.6 the game shows a black screen and closes within seconds. So the first start
  there offers to fetch Microsoft's newer Direct3D 12 runtime (the D3D12 Agility
  SDK, `D3D12Core.dll`, about 22 MB from nuget.org). It goes into a `D3D12`
  folder beside `victory.exe`. `victory.exe get-d3d12` does the same by hand.
  The file is checked against Microsoft's signature and the tested SHA-256.
  Windows 11 keeps using its own runtime. A `D3D12` folder that is already
  there, for example from a repack or another guide (1.618, 1.620), is used
  at the version of its `D3D12Core.dll`. Before v2026.11.27.4 that version
  had to be 1.614, or Windows refused Direct3D 12 with `0x887E0003`.
- C: drive full? Set `VICTORY_HOME` to another folder, once, in a command
  prompt: `setx VICTORY_HOME D:\victory`. Then start victory.exe from a new
  window. Settings, saves, caches, logs and the downloads all go there
  instead of `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory`. To keep what you have, move that
  folder's contents there first.
- You need Windows 10 or 11, 32 GB of RAM or more, an SSD and an NVIDIA
  GeForce RTX card with a recent driver. This repository and its releases
  contain no game files.
- **The first start of each new version restarts by itself once.** A new
  `victory.exe` runs at about 14 fps on its first start, and normally from then
  on. So the first start plays about 20 seconds, says so at the top of the
  picture, and starts the game again. It doesn't happen again for that version
  (a mark is kept in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\warmed`).
- RTX 20 and 30 cards can try DLSS frame generation with the
  [MFG Unlocker](https://github.com/dashdogy/MFG-Unlocker) mod (not ours, and
  not tested with this fork, which was only run on an RTX 50). It is an option,
  off by default: **F1, MFG UNLOCKER, ON**, then restart. On, the next start
  downloads it by itself from the mod's own GitHub release (v1.7.2, about 5 MB,
  checked against the SHA-256 its author published) into
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\victory\mfg-unlocker`, and every start loads it. Nothing is
  renamed or copied. On an RTX 20 or 30 the first start also asks once (No unless
  you type y). `victory.exe get-mfg` downloads it by hand. The mod writes its own

Your safety comes first: sponsors get a logo and a link here, nothing more. No paid recommendations and no setup guides for third-party AI API resellers, so nothing here steers your code, keys or data somewhere you didn't choose.

## Quick start

Paste this into your coding agent:

```text
Install Rust Anything with npm i -g rust-anything, then run rust-anything setup. Run rust-anything go --  and finish the port until rust-anything gate passes.
```

Or install it yourself:

```sh
cargo install rust-anything   # or: npm install -g rust-anything
rust-anything setup           # adds it to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenCode
```

> [!TIP]
> **Agents:** read [rustanything.ai/llms.txt](https://rustanything.ai/llms.txt) for the install steps, every command and the porting workflow.

## How it works

  
    
    
  

**What counts as done.** Behavior, not your tests. `record` runs the original on generated and given inputs and saves what each call returns, throws and prints. A port is done when `gate` passes: every recorded case matches, and fmt, clippy, `cargo test`, the `unsafe` check, the stub check and the check for recorded answers pasted into the port all pass. Your own tests run too.

**Report or migrate, you pick.** `analyze` and `profile` only report: a ranked plan of what to port, and what is hot under a real workload. They are plain commands, so the report costs no tokens. `go` migrates one unit: it bridges the hottest function, records it, hands the port to your agent, then builds, diffs and gates it, and switches it on only when everything matches (TS/JS, Python and PowerShell; `disable` switches it back off).

**How long a run takes.** One `go` run ports one unit, with at most `--rounds` agent turns (3 by default): one for the port, then one per failing diff or gate. A whole app is one run per unit, so you can stop after any of them.

**Cheap model for the plan, strong model for the port.** The plan needs no model. For the port, pass any agent command: `rust-anything go --agent "claude --model " -- `.

## How it works

Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps,
asking you in plain words when a decision is yours:

1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs.
2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your
   request names (or a sensible default).
3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet.
4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

  
    
      
      Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
    
    
      
      Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
    
  

## Two ways to use it

- **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it,
  press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the
  agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and
  buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom.
  "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode).
- **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C,
  disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console.

Both modes drive the same engine.

## Clean room or Deep

- **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page
  source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor
  sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened)
  and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused

- **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the
  built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start
  page watched, and the builder may use all of them.

Clean room is a rule about what Craft Anything offers and refuses. It is not an operating-system
sandbox: it doesn't isolate your computer. A coding agent you run still acts as you, and what it can
read, write or run depends on its own permissions. Which of an agent's own tools Craft Anything can
refuse differs by agent; for Claude Code's tools in chats and questions, see

`--deep` (or `--clean-room`).

oss.readme:
# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can (shaders and pipelines too, see Getting started) and on first use
otherwise. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet, because of the framerate: about 1 frame per second in the
world.** Nothing else keeps the game from working: the title boots, runs its
menus at its own 30 fps, loads the world, plays the intro cutscene and
reaches the **prologue**, the mission after it, with the graphics fully
displayed. 

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about a minute) | works |
| The intro cutscene | plays at about 1 fps (0.9-1.0 s a frame, warm cache, quiet machine): textured and lit characters with whole hair, buildings, sky, depth of field, the title card, credits and interface. Missing: ray-traced shadows and indirect light, the local-light shadow mask. Seen in some shots: a pink band over nearer bodies, a stand-in head on a secondary character for a few frames |
| The prologue | reached; the graphics are fully displayed, at about 1 fps |

In the intro cutscene at 1 fps the opening credits land over other shots than
on a console: they follow the frame count, the shots follow the clock.

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT (12 GB).

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU hung it in earlier builds,
> and Windows then reset the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). The latest runs, several minutes each in the world, did not, but
> it is not ruled out; a run can also end on a GPU fault (`crashes.log`). A
> diagnostics build with `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` renders on the software
> adapter instead (too slow to reach the world in minutes).

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | The scene is drawn and presented: mesh pipelines, indirect execution, views the shaders pick from the heap themselves, title memory read by address, depth written from compute, lists that wait for values other queues write, textures made when a shader first reads them, pipelines pre-built or made by worker threads and kept on disk, depth bounds on supporting adapters (synthetic tests) | The title's ray-tracing structures are never built (no ray-traced shadows or indirect light in the intro cutscene); about 1 s a frame; draws of untranslated shaders are dropped; real queries, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL, ahead of time (`translate --cache`) or at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: all but under 300 of 24,387 programs | Merged geometry stages (195 programs) and under 100 others; fused multiply-adds follow the host GPU; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Menus, loading and the world run with the PC upscaler (`VICTORY_FIDELITYFX_DIR`, about 1 s a frame) | The title's own upscaler DLLs: six of their passes are untranslated, so their picture is wrong |

## Getting started

Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, a CPU with AVX2, a Direct3D 12 GPU with
shader model 6.6 (and mesh shaders for the world), Rust (pinned in
`rust-toolchain.toml`).

To install Rust, use rustup (`winget install --id Rustlang.Rustup -e`, or
the installer from https://rustup.rs). The first `cargo` command in this
repository then fetches the pinned toolchain. Building needs the MSVC C++
build tools: Visual Studio or its Build Tools with the "Desktop development
with C++" workload.

Keep the build paths short. From a checkout about 170 characters deep, the
`blake3` dependency's build script fails in `ml64.exe` with
`A1009: line too long`, even with long paths enabled in Windows, because
its object files land under `target`. Set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to a short
absolute path (`$env:CARGO_TARGET_DIR = 'C:\vt'`; `victory.exe` is then
in `C:\vt\release` instead of `target\release`), or check out the
repository nearer the drive's root.

A run in the world takes about 33 GB of Windows commit (RAM plus paging
file) and about 10 GB of video memory. The tested machine has 32 GB of RAM
and a commit limit of about 80 GB. Check **Committed** under **Task Manager →
Performance → Memory**. If `crashes.log` reports Windows error 1455, close
other applications or increase the Windows paging file size, then retry.

cargo xtask install-hooks                # asset-policy check on every commit
copy victory.example.toml victory.toml   # then set your paths (outside the repo)
cargo test --workspace                   # needs no game data
cargo run -p

releases.name: v4.13.23
releases.body:
## Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

### TrieRouter treats `__proto__` as a registered HTTP method

Affects: applications that use TrieRouter and accept arbitrary method names, for example with HTTP/2 on Node.js or with `hono/method-override`. A request with a method name such as `__proto__` made the router add a property to `Object.prototype`, so later requests in the same process could fail until it was restarted. The router no longer treats an inherited property as a registered method. GHSA-656w-x92q-369m

### `except()` skips a middleware for a path that only starts or ends with an alternative of a constrained parameter

Affects: `except()` in `hono/combine`, with a path condition that has an alternation in a constrained parameter. A path that only started or ended with one of the alternatives also matched the condition, so the middleware did not run for it. The regular expression of a parameter is now grouped, and routes on TrieRouter with such a parameter are corrected by the same change. GHSA-586x-c76g-h528

### `getPath()` drops the first path segment when the request URL has no scheme and host

Affects: applications on Bun that rely on path rules of a reverse proxy to protect routes. Bun gives a URL with only the path for a request without a usable `Host` header, and Hono dropped the first segment of the path before routing, so a request could reach a route that the proxy blocks by path. The path of such a URL is now read correctly. GHSA-mhwf-w6q6-q58w

---

Users who use TrieRouter with HTTP/2 on Node.js or `hono/method-override`, `except()` with a constrained parameter, or Bun behind a reverse proxy are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/honojs/hono/compare/v4.13.22...v4.13.23

releases.body:
### Minor Changes

- [#17183](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/17183) [`ebc7b50`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/ebc7b509c659bef9ad413112f0907b8f815eae22) Thanks [@gpanders](https://github.com/gpanders)! - Accept `linux/arm64` images in `wrangler containers push` and `wrangler containers build`

  `wrangler containers push` now accepts local images built for `linux/amd64` or `linux/arm64`. `wrangler containers build --platform` accepts the same two platforms. The default platform is still `linux/amd64`.

- [#17088](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/17088) [`43da328`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/43da3289c5f715c03143d31fde6dc46b4d90b28b) Thanks [@efalcao](https://github.com/efalcao)! - Add the `oidc_tokens` binding

  An OIDC token binding issues short-lived OpenID Connect tokens for the Worker's own identity, for one audience. Exchange them for cloud credentials, or send them to an API as a bearer token, instead of storing long-lived credentials as secrets:

  ```jsonc
  "oidc_tokens": [{ "binding": "API_TOKEN", "audience": "https://api.example.com" }]
  ```

  `env.API_TOKEN.getToken()` returns a newly signed JWT. Set `"alg": "RS256"` for verifiers that don't accept the default, ES256. Wrangler validates the audience (1 to 2048 printable ASCII characters, no whitespace), uploads the binding, generates its `OidcTokenBinding` type, and prints it in the bindings table. After a deploy, `wrangler deploy` prints the issuer and subject to put in the verifier's trust policy. The subject contains the Worker's immutable ID, which the deploy output doesn't otherwise show. The binding isn't available in local development yet. Accounts must be enabled for the binding before they can deploy it.

- [#17161](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/17161) [`e46c7c6`](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/e46c7c6a4c9c797f5d8f40827c9f2e4ef8e3fd6c) Thanks [@thisisamank](https://github.com/thisisamank)! - Add RealtimeKit bindings

  Bind an existing RealtimeKit app to a Worker in your Wrangler configuration file:

  ```jsonc
  {
    "realtimekit": [
      {
        "binding": "RTK",
        "app_id": "<APP_ID>",
        "remote": true
      }
    ]
  }
  ```

  RealtimeKit has no local simulator, so set `remote: true` to use the real app during local development. Calls during development, including calls on returned meetings, go through the existing remote bindings proxy. The experimental configuration API supports `bindings.realtimeKit({ id: "<APP_ID>", dev: { remote: true } })`, and the `wrangler-to-cf` codemod converts `realtimekit` entries. Deployments upload only the binding name and `app_id`. `wrangler types` generates `RealtimeKitBinding` for these bindings.
